# T0.19 — packaging v8 (suite tsvc_c4: the contrast set's loops and s341 on data that move) on the server, before a model reads it

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done

## The question

Are the nine tsvc_c4 packages sound to measure on — built alike on both machines, at a measurable size, each reference verified and faster — which of the eight new loops does DiscoPoP alone parallelize (the control) and which does it leave unchanged (the set under test), and is s341 on its new data the loop DiscoPoP saw before?

## Result in one paragraph

No model (10 Oct). The nine tsvc_c4 packages are built alike on both machines (45 files, every digest equal), each at a measurable size, each reference verified correct and FASTER by the harness (4.1x to 28.3x at 12 threads on the new loops; s341 2.4x). DiscoPoP alone, three draws: it parallelizes one of the eight new loops itself (s311, the plain sum, 8.3x) and leaves seven unchanged — the five extreme-value loops and the coupled sum s319 (nothing offered), and the conditional sum s3111, whose pragma it offers and the agent's output check refuses in 3 of 3 (a reordered sum differs in the 15th digit where the check compares byte for byte). Given the reference of an extreme-value loop with its directives removed, DiscoPoP writes none on any of the five. s341 on its new data is the loop DiscoPoP saw before (two draws, every criterion the same); the form that computes the positions once reproduces the output on the data of every earlier run and changes it on the new data.

`s314` (largest value), `s316` (smallest value), `s3113` (largest absolute value) — the reference is TSVC's loop with one clause, `reduction(max:…)` or `reduction(min:…)`; `s315` (largest value and the first index holding it), `s318` (the same on absolute values at a stride) — no clause exists for the pair; the reference keeps a pair per thread and merges them under a lock. Five loops expected under test, not eight; said to the author with the files. **Packaging v8 is v7** (the repetition loop inside the function, `dummy` recording every repetition and handed the number the repetition computed) **with:** (a) *data in which each new loop's result moves between repetitions*, as v7 gave `s331`: `dummy` adds 0.25 to one element of `a` per call at positions the measurement header knows; a ladder of values on those positions spanning less than 0.25 makes the element just raised the new largest (`s314`, `s315`, `s318`, `s3113`: 2.0 + 0.005·n) or makes the smallest element the one raised next (`s316`: −2.0 + 0.005·n); `a[0]`, which `dummy` raises by 0.125 per call, overtakes the ladder after about a quarter of the repetitions and is the largest from then on. On the shipped input the result is a new value in every repetition; on the perturbed input the ladder is no longer in order (the perturbation scales each element by up to a fifth, after the data are set), so the result need not change at every call there — what is PROVEN, on both inputs, is that the variants `skip` and `reorder` change the output (the generator's validation). `s3111` gets negative elements so that its test decides something. The sums move by themselves. (b) *`s341` on other data:* the elements of `b` that `dummy` raises start at −0.1, so one more element is positive in every repetition and every later position of the packed array shifts. (c) *a third variant the generator proves wrong for `s341`* (`hoist`): the form of every program that won this loop in E1-v6 and E3 with its directive removed — the positions computed once, in front of the repetitions. (d) three details of the files a model reads: `ABS`, which TSVC defines as `fabs` in `common.h`, is defined in `data.h` with `#include <math.h>` (`s318`, `s3113`); `s318`'s stride `inc` is a hidden value as `s171`'s (TSVC's driver passes 1); and from `s315` the two lines with which TSVC's own function fills `a` in front of the repetitions are removed — data set-up, which is the measurement header's here (with them the function would overwrite the header's data and the perturbed input). The generator's change is confined to a new suite: `tsvc_c2` and `tsvc_c3` regenerate byte for byte after it (compared with the baseline taken at `0c7723749`). **Proven on the Mac, in a scratch folder** (`prepare_tsvc.py --layout v8 --suite tsvc_c4 --validate`): 9 of 9 packages validated — output finite, changed by the perturbed input, deterministic; the reference equal to the original on both inputs at 4 threads; the variants `skip` and `reorder` change the output on both inputs for every package; `hoist` changes `s341`'s output on both inputs (largest relative difference 0.885 and 0.906).
